Substructure: The steel or aluminium frame between the building and the stone fixings.
Up-Down angle: An angle with one tongue up into the panel above and one down into the panel below.
Kerf: A slot sawn along the panel edge to receive a blade or tongue.
Kerf rail: A rail whose blade sits in the kerf, locally or continuously.
Undercut anchor: An anchor locked by shape into a widened hole in the back of the panel.
Hanger: The clasp on an undercut anchor that hooks onto the horizontal rail.
Loadbearing fixing: A fixing that carries the weight of the panel.
Restraint fixing: A fixing that holds the panel against wind but carries no weight.
Pull-out test: A site test that loads an installed anchor to a proof load.
Mock-up: A sample area built before the work, approved as the benchmark.
Shop drawings: Drawings that show every panel, fixing and detail as it will be built.
Material submittal: Data and samples submitted for the consultant's approval.
Method statement: The written sequence and controls for the work.
Inspection and test plan: The list of checks, criteria, records and hold points.
ITP: The list of checks, criteria, records and hold points.
Hold point: A stage where work stops until the consultant releases it.
Witness point: A stage the consultant is invited to witness.
Non-conformance report: The record of work that does not match the approved documents.
NCR: The record of work that does not match the approved documents.
Movement joint: A joint that lets the facade move with temperature and the structure.
Open joint: A joint left unsealed in a ventilated facade.
Ventilated cavity: The air space behind the stone.
Fixed point: Where a member is held, and where it is free to move with temperature.
sliding point: Where a member is held, and where it is free to move with temperature.
Shims: Thin packers used to adjust a bracket; stainless steel or plastic.
Isolator: A washer or pad that separates two different metals.
Hot-dip galvanised: Steel coated with zinc by dipping after fabrication.
Wind load: Pressure and suction from wind, calculated for each project to SBC 301.
Safety factor: The factor applied to tested strength to obtain an allowable value.
Flexural strength: The bending strength of the stone, from tests.
Lippage: The step between the faces of two adjacent panels.
Tolerance: The permitted deviation in line, level, plumb and joint width.
Efflorescence: White salt deposits on the face, usually from cement mortar and moisture.
Back mesh: Mesh bonded to the back of a panel to hold fragments if it breaks.
European Technical Assessment: A published assessment of a construction product, such as an undercut anchor.
ETA: A published assessment of a construction product, such as an undercut anchor.
